classification.difficultyReason: Models vertical displacement from an elevated launch and selects the positive quadratic root.

content.prompt:
Michele throws a frisbee from a window $15.3\text{ m}$ up.
The initial speed is $8.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at an angle of $73^\circ$ above the horizontal.
Find the time taken to reach the ground, to $1$ decimal place. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

answer.worked:
Take the origin at the window, with upwards positive.
$$\begin{aligned}\dot{x}&=8.8\cos73^\circ\\\dot{y}&=-10t+8.8\sin73^\circ\\y&=-5t^2+(8.8\sin73^\circ)t\end{aligned}$$
At the ground, $y=-15.3$.
$$\begin{aligned}-15.3&=-5t^2+(8.8\sin73^\circ)t\\5t^2-(8.8\sin73^\circ)t-15.3&=0\\t&=\frac{8.8\sin73^\circ\pm\sqrt{(8.8\sin73^\circ)^2+4(5)(15.3)}}{10}\end{aligned}$$
Taking the positive root gives $t\approx2.8\text{ s}$.
